name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=y(x-3)^{3}.$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$

| $y>0$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ |  |  |
|  | $x<3$ | $x>3$ |
worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=3$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/6b88b092c69226e8590547f6cf1c27fb5046006c6d24516c8a112ea5ae5fe665.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/9ce50d0e01602f4c28666444df79e9feb98312338b2fe11a2760d7587ea5a548.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $y$ | $(x-3)^{3}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(2,1)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(4,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(2,-1)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(4,-1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/f03e23b1a5f1bc4faf478d0a14c90d4bc2f24f5e56a61e9708dd7339ff5558e6.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>0$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ | $+$ | $-$ |
|  | $x<3$ | $x>3$ |
